# CAN as a Service: One Bus Owner, Named Participants

Design for #146. This document settles the questions the issue lists; the
implementation follows it in phases. Nothing here changes existing
single-owner configurations.

## Problem

A `can_buses` entry models the bus as a device with a single owner:
`can:<adapter>:<channel>` is one exclusive, machine-wide lock. CAN is a shared
medium. Several devices under test on one physical bus is the ordinary case,
and several projects testing against the same bus is the ordinary bench. The
current model serialises all of them against one lock and cannot express
sharing at all.

## Shape

One broker process owns one physical bus. It takes the existing exclusive bus
lock (the same key runs take today) and holds it for its lifetime, so
everything the single-owner model enforces keeps being enforced, by one
process, exactly once. It opens the adapter once.

Participants are named connections to the broker. Each attaches under
`<bus-key>#<name>`, carries its own identifier filter and frame view, and
declares itself in a run the way a device does today. Runs in different
projects share the bus by each holding a participant connection, not by
racing for the device lock.

## Rules

### Locking

- The physical bus lock lives in the broker. A machine where no broker runs
  behaves exactly as today.
- Participants take logical participant locks (`<bus-key>#<name>`), so two
  runs may not share one participant name, while any number of distinctly
  named participants proceed in parallel.

The broker is implemented in **`src/agentic_hil/canbroker.py`**, specifically the `CanBroker` class (defined around line 519):

```python
class CanBroker:
    """One process, one physical bus, many named participants.

    Owns the bus lock and the adapter for its whole life. Everything a
    participant does to the medium passes through here, which is what makes the
    whole-bus frame log complete: the broker is the only writer, so a frame in a
    participant's own log is a frame in this one, under the same sequence
    number."""
```

This class:
- Owns a single physical CAN bus, holding the machine-wide exclusive lock for its entire lifetime (`take_bus`), and opens the adapter once (`open_bus`).
- Exposes an IPC endpoint (via `multiprocessing.connection.Listener`) so multiple separate processes/runs can attach as **named participants** rather than each trying to open the physical device themselves.
- Serves those participants (`serve` method) until shutdown.

The module also provides:
- `main()` — the CLI entry point (`agentic-hil-can-broker`) that starts a `CanBroker` for a given `bus_id`.
- `attach_participant` — the client-side function participants use to connect to a running broker (referenced in `tests/test_can_broker.py`).

The design rationale is documented in `docs/can-service-design.md` ("CAN as a Service: One Bus Owner, Named Participants"), which states: "One broker process owns one physical bus... Participants are named connections to the broker... Runs in different projects share the bus by each holding a participant connection, not by racing for the device lock."

Related config types live in `src/agentic_hil/types.py` (`CanShareConfig`), describing the per-participant "share" view (filters, permissions, frame budget) of a shared bus.
